hook: What if a river could carve through 300 million years of rock?

sections.voiceover: What if a river could carve through 300 million years of rock?
On October 6, 2026, the International Space Station photographed the San Juan River in Utah. How did the San Juan River slice through 300 million years of ancient stone?
Geologic forces pushed the Colorado Plateau upward starting 20 million years ago, forcing the river downward.
At Goosenecks State Park in Utah, the San Juan River carved a canyon 300 meters deep.
NASA Earth Observatory released the International Space Station's photograph on November 6, 2026.
